key_insight: K2SnGeX6 and Rb2SnGeX6 lead-free double perovskites are predicted by DFT to be structurally stable, ductile, and highly tunable in bandgap and thermoelectric performance across Cl/Br/I substitution.
engineering_relevance: The chloride variants suit photovoltaic absorber design, while the bromide/iodide variants are promising for tandem PV, near-IR photodetectors, and high-ZT waste-heat recovery devices.
method: DFT calculations of formation energy, band structure, optical response, and thermoelectric transport
Mechanical-property analysis from elastic constants to assess ductility and processability
Stability screening using tolerance and octahedral factors for cubic perovskite compatibility
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a direct bandgap range of 1.44 to 0.64 eV and a peak thermoelectric figure of merit of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: These are computational predictions only, so experimental synthesis, phase stability, and device-level validation are still needed before deployment.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
